title: Dairy-Free Lavender Vanilla Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft dairy-free vanilla cupcakes with real lavender flavor, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes use dairy-free milk and butter, so anyone avoiding dairy can enjoy them without missing out. The lavender comes from steeped culinary buds, not extract, so the flavor stays soft and floral, never soapy. I tested three lavender amounts before landing on the right one. Too much and it tastes like potpourri, too little and you cannot taste it at all. The white swirl frosting sits on top like a little cloud and lets the pale purple crumb peek through underneath.
ingredients: 1 cup unsweetened dairy-free milk (oat or almond)
1/3 cup dairy-free butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Warm the 1 cup dairy-free milk in a small saucepan until it steams, then remove from heat.
Stir in the lavender buds and let steep for 15 minutes, then strain out the buds and cool the milk.
Preheat oven to 350°F and line a muffin pan with 12 paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a medium bowl.
Beat the 1/2 cup dairy-free butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each, then mix in the vanilla.
Alternate adding the flour mix and the cooled lavender milk, starting and ending with flour, mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among liners and bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat the frosting butter until creamy, then add powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla, beating until fluffy and smooth.
Pipe the frosting in a tall swirl on each cooled cupcake.
tips: Buy culinary grade lavender only. Garden or craft lavender can taste bitter and is not meant for food.
Steep the milk covered so the lavender oils do not evaporate before they flavor the milk.
Strain the lavender well. Leftover buds in the batter can taste gritty and too strong.
If your frosting looks too soft to pipe a tall swirl, chill it in the fridge for 10 minutes first.

faq.question: Can I use lavender extract instead of dried buds?
faq.answer: Yes, use 1/4 teaspoon lavender extract added to the batter instead of steeping milk. Start with less and taste, since extracts vary in strength.

faq.question: Why does my lavender taste soapy?
faq.answer: Soapy flavor usually means too much lavender or non-culinary buds. Stick to the 1 tablespoon amount and use buds labeled for baking.

faq.question: What dairy-free butter works best for the frosting?
faq.answer: A stick-style dairy-free butter with at least 70% fat pipes best. Spreadable tub versions can make the frosting too soft to hold a swirl.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost the same day you plan to serve them.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove dairy-free baking can still taste delicate and special. The lavender stays soft in the background, not front and center, so it works even for guests who think they do not like floral desserts. Give them a try for a spring bake or a calm afternoon treat.
